slides.text: My guild does not map the living world. We use ink ground from meteor iron and phoenix ash on vellum that remains blank until an empire falls. Only when a city is erased from the earth does the parchment drink the ink, sketching every vanished spire, tavern, and cobblestone in luminous silver so history cannot be murdered twice.

For forty years, my great atlas lay silent on its oak lectern. Then, at midnight during the winter festival, I heard the dry scratch of an invisible quill. My master sheet was bleeding silver ink at a frantic pace. Street by familiar street, canal by canal, the parchment was drawing Vaelen—our own capital city—while the bells outside were still ringing with laughter.

I ran to the window, expecting fire in the sky, but the stars were calm. When I looked back at the table, the phantom ink had finished the palace walls and was drawing a single, glowing gold line threading from my workshop door, through the catacombs, out to the sea. Beside it, in my late master's handwriting, three words appeared: 'Wake the children.'
